hook.line: Someone you have never heard of is asking about you. You want to say so, with just a hint of "and who is he?". Spanish has two small words for that.
hook.en: Some guy called Camilo was looking for you. (to a friend)

examples.es: Me lo dijo una tal Marcela.

examples.en: Some guy called Camilo was looking for you. (to a friend)

examples.es: Vino una tal Lucía a preguntar por ti.
examples.en: A certain Lucía came to ask about you. (to a friend)

examples.es: Compró el edificio un tal Ramírez.
examples.en: A certain Ramírez bought the building.

examples.es: Lo firmó un tal doctor Peña.
examples.en: A certain Dr Peña signed it.

rule:
*Un tal* or *una tal* plus a name means "a certain" or "some guy called". It says: I don't know this person, and I'm not sure you do either. It can sound a little dismissive.

It matches the person: *un tal Camilo* for a man, *una tal Lucía* for a woman.

Use it for someone who has not been introduced. Once you know who it is, drop *tal* and just say the name: *Camilo*.

A title can come after *tal*: *un tal doctor Peña*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the indefinite article with *tal* used as an adjective meaning "called".

options: A certain Rodríguez called, a stranger to me.
Rodríguez, our neighbour, called.
I called Rodríguez.

readAndPick.es: Me lo dijo una tal Marcela.
options: Marcela, my sister, told me.
I told a certain Marcela.
A certain Marcela told me.
Camilo, your friend, was looking for you.
Some guy called Camilo was looking for you. (to a friend)
I was looking for a certain Camilo.

readAndPick.es: Vino una tal Lucía a preguntar por ti.
options: A certain Lucía came to ask about you. (to a friend)
Lucía, your sister, came to ask about you.
A certain Lucía asked about me.

readAndPick.es: Compró el edificio un tal Ramírez.
options: Ramírez bought a certain building.
The building bought a certain Ramírez.
A certain Ramírez bought the building.

readAndPick.es: Lo firmó un tal doctor Peña.
options: Dr Peña, our doctor, signed it.
A certain Dr Peña signed it.
I signed it for Dr Peña.

readAndPick.es: Ayer llamó una tal Paula del banco.
options: Yesterday I called a certain Paula from the bank.
Yesterday Paula from the bank called me, as always.
Yesterday a certain Paula from the bank called.

readAndPick.es: Mariana dice que habló con una tal Diana.
options: Mariana says she spoke with a certain Diana.
Mariana says Diana spoke with her.
Mariana says she spoke with her friend Diana.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *un tal* or *una tal* and type the whole sentence: *Te buscaba ___ Camilo.*
yourTurn.why: Camilo is a man, so *un tal*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: A certain Marcela told me.
yourTurn.answer: Me lo dijo una tal Marcela.
yourTurn.why: Marcela is a woman, so *una tal*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: A certain Ramírez bought the building.
yourTurn.answer: Compró el edificio un tal Ramírez.
accept: Un tal Ramírez compró el edificio.
yourTurn.why: *Un tal* goes right before the name.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: A certain Dr Peña signed it.
yourTurn.answer: Lo firmó un tal doctor Peña.
yourTurn.why: The title comes after *tal* and before the name.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a woman: *Te buscaba un tal Camilo.* Say: A certain Lucía was looking for you.
yourTurn.why: Both little words change to feminine: *una tal*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Yesterday a certain Paula from the bank called.
yourTurn.answer: Ayer llamó una tal Paula del banco.
accept: Llamó ayer una tal Paula del banco.
yourTurn.why: The caller is a woman you don't know, so *una tal*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Mariana says she spoke with a certain Diana.
yourTurn.answer: Mariana dice que habló con una tal Diana.
yourTurn.why: *Con una tal Diana* keeps the same frame after *con*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish needs *un* before *tal*, where English only needs "a certain".
Almost. *Tal* matches the person, so a woman gets *una tal*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me lo dijo una tal Marcela, mi hermana.
pitfalls.right: Me lo dijo Marcela, mi hermana.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Una tal* means a stranger, so for someone you know, just say the name.

personal: Imagine someone you don't know called the café today, and say who: *Llamó un tal…* or *una tal…*.
